text: {"domains":{"block_M":[16,32],"block_N":[64,128,256],"block_K":[32,64,128],"num_stages":[2,3,4],"threads":[64,128],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16,32,64]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1.0,"launches":1.0,"pipeline":1.5,"footprint":0.5},"rationale":"Fourth-round plan for M=32,N=4096,K=4096. History: attempt-00 195.8us (256thr,3st), attempt-01 176.4us (256thr,2st), attempt-02 147.6us (128thr,3st) — all passed numerics/compile, DRAM flat ~33.8MB so panel locality never materialized; swizzles remain launch-equivalent with ceil(M/block_M) in {1,2}. Threads reduced to 128 improved latency, so we probe 64 threads (untested branch) while keeping 128 as the incumbent; block_M stays [16,32] since larger tiles waste M rows and small M needs blocks for occupancy; block_N spans 64..256 (attempt-02 used 64; worth testing wider N with fewer launches); block_K [32,64,128] kept broad since only 64 has been measured; stages [2,3,4] as stage 1 rarely helps K=4096; swizzle expanded again but expected launch-equivalent. Weights kept from attempt-02 (pipeline 1.5, footprint 0.5) since flat DRAM confirms latency is pipeline/occupancy-bound rather than traffic-bound. Shared estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*stages, 4*block_M*block_N) under 32768 cap and portability limit. Next hypothesis: 64 threads and/or larger block_N with 3-4 stages may reduce simulated latency; if 64-thread regresses revert to 128. GB10 values are simulator-only estimates; Metal checks validate exact source/TIR but do not execute the CUDA binary. No global optimality claimed."}
